source: derived from the chain records' chokepoint fields

rows.physics: Single-crystal blades are HOT but BATCH — concentrated by qualification + know-how, not power
Hall–Héroult runs non-stop; a potline freezes solid if power drops — one big unit at cheap power

basis.text: International Aluminium Institute (IAI): China's share of world primary aluminium smelting, ~59%. Limit: IAI aggregates member and estimated output — it is not a customs or USGS figure, and smelter output is a different position from bauxite mining or alumina refining.

rows.physics: Continuous high-temp, high-pressure synthesis; gas is feedstock + energy → sites at cheap gas
Trioxide + metal refining — China built the capacity; the mine diversified but refining didn't

basis.text: Anchored on public sources. USGS MCS 2026 shows the MINE is diversifying — China ~36% (40,000 of 110,000 t, 2025e), with Russia and Tajikistan now large — so the mine is not the chokepoint. The binding stage is refining: Reuters (Aug 2024) states China 'is the biggest supplier of refined antimony' while it imports its ore, and Project Blue notes feedstock — not refining capacity — is the constraint; USGS confirms the direction via US imports (antimony oxide 66% China). Limit: no source publishes a single world refined-antimony share, so the page asserts refining dominance qualitatively ('refine'), not a percentage — industry places China at ~75-90% of processing, though IEA GCMO 2026 gives a notably lower 44% share of refining — the spread itself shows why this is not a settled number.

rows.physics: A by-product of copper/gold smelting — recovered from toxic flue dust, not mined; supply bounded by the host and by nobody wanting to make it
A cheap, heavy, abundant weighting mineral mined near demand (India/China/Morocco) — no chokepoint, but you can't drill without it
Electrode coating + cell assembly at scale — capital + process capability, ~80% China

basis.text: IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026: China produced ~80% of global battery cells in 2025 (also 98% of LFP cathode, ~95% of cathode precursors, over 90% of anode material). The atlas uses ~80% for the cell-manufacturing chokepoint. Limit: cell-output share; capacity is expanding fast outside China (US/Korea LFP lines), and this is the manufacturing stage, not the upstream mineral refining.

rows.physics: Hard-won hydrometallurgy + alloying, guarded by toxicity — concentrated in the US, the non-China chokepoint
A by-product of lead and tungsten smelting; China ~88% of production and refining — coupled to hosts, and China dominates the refining

Turkey's borate basins (tincal, colemanite) are a geological rarity concentrated in one region and can't be relocated; its state producer Eti Maden claims ~73% of world reserves, though USGS publishes no consistent world total

basis.text: Eti Maden (Turkey's state boron company) figure: Turkey holds the majority of world borate reserves and production, ~73%. USGS MCS 2026 confirms Turkey is the leading producer (and 90% of US boron imports) but states outright that 'World totals cannot be calculated because production and reserves are not reported in a consistent manner by all countries' — so it prints no world denominator. Limit: a ~73% 'of world' figure cannot come from USGS; it rests on the state company's own number, not an independent primary source.

rows.physics: Limestone + kilns are everywhere and cement is cheap + heavy → made locally; no chokepoint, only CO₂
Ferrochrome is ~40% power by cost — the furnace follows cheap electricity (KZ/CN)
A by-product of Congolese copper; can't be mined alone, then refined in China

basis.text: IEA / industry: China's share of refined, battery-grade cobalt, ~75% — regardless of where the ore was mined (mining is a separate ~75% DR Congo figure, which IS measured). Limit: the refining share is agency-compiled, not a quoted USGS table row.

rows.physics: Mining is diversified and switchable; the limit is TIME — a decade to open a mine
Power + grid connection are local and switchable — the limit is megawatts, not one country
A composite — inherits its inputs' China-processed capability (magnets, gallium, antimony, tungsten)
Refined electrolytically at MODEST temp — concentrated because it rides on zinc, not by heat
The scale limit is iridium — a trace by-product of platinum mining (future-tense)

basis.text: Qualitative — no single national share. The scale limit for PEM electrolysers is iridium, a trace by-product of South African platinum mining. Limit: this is a materials-scaling constraint, not a country-concentration percentage.

rows.physics: Assembly is switchable and localises near demand; the real chokepoint is upstream (battery/magnet)

basis.text: IEA Global EV Outlook: China assembled ~16M of ~22M electric cars in 2025 (~70%). Limit: this is a production-location share that localises behind tariffs and shifts yearly; assembly is not the real chokepoint (the battery and magnet chains are).

rows.physics: Vapour-deposition preform-making — a few firms hold the process know-how
Fluorspar → HF → fluorochemicals; the gateway chemical, ~60% China
Trace by-product of alumina/zinc refining — bounded by the host, not gallium demand
By-product of zinc residues + coal fly ash — can't scale on its own; USGS states producers do not publicly report germanium output, so the share is an estimate

basis.text: IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026 gives China ~94% of germanium (2025). Earlier commonly-cited figures were lower (~60%), and USGS confirms China is 'the leading global producer' but states germanium output is not publicly reported and estimates are 'difficult to verify' — so it publishes no share. The atlas uses ~90% to reflect the IEA figure while flagging the by-product data as murky. Limit: germanium is a poorly-measured zinc/coal by-product; sources range ~60-94%.

rows.physics: Spheronising + purifying + coating flake into anode — ~95% China

basis.text: IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026: China produces 'over 90% of anode material' and ~94% of refined graphite (2025). The uncoated spherical-graphite precursor step specifically approaches ~100% China (Benchmark Mineral Intelligence), but finished anode material is ~90-95%; mined flake graphite is ~74% China. The atlas uses ~95% for the anode chokepoint. Limit: the exact figure depends on which processing step (spherical precursor vs coated anode).

rows.physics: Batch-built equipment; the limit is factory lead-time (years), spread across suppliers
No scarce input; the limit is factory capacity + installer labour — a labour market
By-product of helium-rich natural gas; coupled to a few fields, non-renewable
~60% of lead is recycled from spent batteries, locally — a closed loop, not a geographic chokepoint
Converting spodumene/brine to battery-grade chemical — the concentrated step, China

basis.text: IEA: China does most of the world's lithium-chemical conversion (spodumene/brine to battery-grade), even though mining is diversified (Australia, Chile). 'Most' is roughly 60-70% in sources. Limit: the conversion share is agency-estimated, not USGS-tabulated.

rows.physics: Coal-fired Pidgeon retorts, energy-sited in one Chinese province

basis.text: Computed from the atlas's own BGS/USGS production series: China sat around 85-88% of primary magnesium across 2019-2023, so ~87%. Limit: the reliable public series is short; this point figure is our read of that series, pending a single clean primary quote.

rows.physics: Solvent-extraction separation of chemically-alike elements — an industrial base, ~91% China

basis.text: IEA and Adamas Intelligence: China's share of rare-earth separation and refining — the real magnet chokepoint — is ~91%. Limit: separation share is derived from proprietary industry data; published figures cluster 85-92%.

rows.physics: High-purity manganese sulphate + electrolytic metal — ~95% China

basis.text: IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026 shows China at ~95-97% of refined battery-grade manganese (high-purity sulphate + electrolytic metal) in 2025 — virtually all recent supply growth came from China. Mining is diversified (South Africa, Gabon, Australia). Limit: applies only to the refined battery-grade stage; the ~95% is read from IEA's refined-production chart.

rows.physics: Mo-99 is made in a handful of ageing research reactors; a 66-hour half-life means no stockpile is possible — an irreplaceable, buffer-less capability

basis.text: OECD-NEA: most of the world's molybdenum-99 (which decays to the imaging isotope Tc-99m) is irradiated in roughly six ageing research reactors. Limit: this is a count of major suppliers, not a market share, and the number shifts as reactors retire or restart.

rows.physics: About half a by-product of copper mining (the rest primary); diversified across Chile/China/US/Peru — coupled, but not a severe chokepoint
By-product of steel-plant air separation — captured, not made

basis.text: Industry and press reporting: Ukraine supplied roughly half of the world's semiconductor-grade neon before 2022. Limit: neon is not in USGS statistics; the figure is industry-reported and was heavily disrupted by the 2022 war — a moving target, not a stable share.

rows.physics: Indonesia's raw-ore export BAN forced (China-financed) domestic smelting — built by a rule
Centrifuge enrichment — a licensed service; Russia the largest

basis.text: Russia holds the single largest share of world uranium-enrichment (SWU) capacity, roughly 35-45% (World Nuclear Association / industry). IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026 corroborates the concentration: the top three countries account for ~70% of conversion and enrichment capacity, with Russia the largest. Limit: enrichment is a licensed service measured in separative work units, not a mined commodity; 'largest' is a plurality, not a majority.

rows.physics: The platinum-group ore is in South Africa's Bushveld Complex (~83% of world PGM reserves); SA leads platinum (~71% of mine output) but palladium is Russia-led
~68% of world reserves are in Morocco (though only ~13% of current production); no substitute for phosphorus
Separating 15+ chemically-alike elements is a vast solvent-extraction industrial base — ~90% China, gating the whole basket, not just magnets

basis.text: IEA / industry: China's share of rare-earth separation capacity is ~90%. Limit: this is a separation-capacity figure from industry data; the mined share is lower and more diversified (US, Australia, Myanmar).

rows.physics: A by-product of a by-product — recovered from molybdenum roasting, itself a copper by-product; one of the rarest metals, and it gates single-crystal turbine blades
Advanced photoresist is ~90% Japan; process gases, CMP slurries and EUV pellicles are each held by a few qualified suppliers

basis.text: SEMI / industry: Japan supplies ~90% of the most advanced photoresists. Limit: this applies to leading-edge resist specifically — other inputs (process gases, CMP slurries, EUV pellicles) have their own, different concentrations.

rows.physics: Batch lithography; barrier is decades of process know-how + a single EUV supplier
~70% a by-product of lead/zinc/copper/gold — output bounded by the base metals, can't scale to demand
Polysilicon + wafer pulling are power- and capital-hungry, sited at cheap Chinese power

basis.text: BNEF / IEA: China's share of polysilicon and wafer manufacturing is ~95% at the wafer step. Limit: wafer is the most concentrated stage; cell and module are somewhat less concentrated, and the figures are capacity-based and industry-compiled.

rows.physics: Continuous coke-fired reduction; gated by coking coal + energy

basis.text: worldsteel 2025 crude-steel production: China 960,810 of world 1,850,279 thousand tonnes = 51.9% -> ~52% (was ~54% on 2024 data; China's share has been declining). Limit: this is a crude-volume share from the authoritative industry body (not USGS) — the real chokepoint is coking coal and energy, and downstream alloy / specialty steel is far more diversified.

rows.physics: Niobium is essentially one Brazilian mine (CBMM) — Brazil is ~93% of world mine production, Canada ~7%
A small celestite-mineral market spread across Iran, China, Spain and Mexico — moderately concentrated, no severe chokepoint
A by-product of oil/gas desulfurization + smelting; bounded by fossil-fuel processing, so decarbonization shrinks it
~68% from DRC/Rwanda artisanal mining — a conflict-mineral supply, not a unique deposit
An extreme by-product — recovered from the anode slimes of copper refining; supply is bounded by copper, and it is among the rarest metals recovered at scale
Concentrated + conflict-linked (Myanmar Wa, 3TG); the ore feed is the fragile part

basis.text: USGS end-use + International Tin Association: about half of tin demand is solder, and supply is concentrated in China / Indonesia and conflict-linked (Myanmar's Wa State). Limit: '~half' is a use-share, not a concentration share; the governance chokepoint is the ore feed, which no single percentage captures.

rows.physics: Kroll sponge + qualified aerospace mill — batch, certification-gated (VSMPO etc.)
Mine + APT + carbide processing; ~79% China (67,000 of 85,000 t, 2025) — stable near 80%+ for decades
Recovered from vanadium-bearing iron ore + steel slag — rides on China's steel
A steel-and-concrete machine; the limit is scale/logistics + OEM share, and it localises

basis.text: GWEC: China-headquartered OEMs supplied about two-thirds of new turbines in 2025 (~67%). Limit: this is a supplier-unit share; most turbines are built and sold near where they operate, so it is corporate concentration, not a materials chokepoint.

rows.physics: The host: gallium, germanium, indium and cadmium are recovered at zinc smelters — refining capacity (China ~half) gates them, not just zinc

basis.text: From USGS smelter-production figures: China does roughly half of world zinc smelting — which matters because gallium, germanium, indium and cadmium are recovered there. Limit: '~half' rounds the USGS smelter series; what actually gates the minor metals is the by-product recovery share, which is not separately published.

rows.physics: Nuclear-grade (hafnium-free) zirconium sponge + cladding is a qualified capability held by a few; Zr and Hf are chemical twins, hard to separate

basis.text: Our assessment. Nuclear-grade (hafnium-free) zirconium sponge and cladding is a qualified capability held by a few producers (France, US, Russia, China). Limit: this is a capability count, not a market share — there is no clean public tonnage split.
